knowledge-base.triggers: shell, bash, sh, zsh, .sh, .bash, .zsh, Makefile, CI/CD, pipeline, script, shellcheck, shfmt, bats, shellspec, cron, automation, set -euo pipefail, shebang, posix
knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific guardrails and patterns for Shell/Bash scripting. Loaded when agents work on .sh, .bash, or .zsh files, Makefiles, or CI/CD pipeline scripts. Applies to Bash 4+, POSIX sh, and automation scripts.

core-principles.principle: Every script starts with set -euo pipefail to fail fast on errors.
All variable expansions must be double-quoted to prevent word splitting and globbing.
Use [[ ]] for conditionals, local for function variables, named constants for magic values.
Never swallow errors silently; use trap for cleanup and meaningful exit codes.
All scripts pass shellcheck with zero warnings before commit.

guardrail.rule: Every script must start with #!/usr/bin/env bash followed immediately by set -euo pipefail.
Always double-quote variable expansions: "$var", "$@", "${arr[@]}", "$(command)". Never omit quotes except in arithmetic contexts.
guardrail.bad: grep -r $pattern $directory for arg in $@; do process $arg; done
guardrail.good: grep -r "$pattern" "$directory" for arg in "$@"; do process "$arg"; done

guardrail.rule: Never use eval. Use arrays for dynamic command building instead.
Never hardcode secrets in script files. No hardcoded /tmp paths — use mktemp and trap for cleanup.
guardrail.good: # Read from environment or secret manager tmpfile="$(mktemp)" || exit 1 trap 'rm -f "$tmpfile"' EXIT

guardrail.rule: All scripts must pass shellcheck with zero warnings before commit. Suppress only with a justification comment citing the SC code.
guardrail.good: # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # Variable used by sourced script unused_looking_var="value"

guardrail.rule: All variables inside functions must be declared local. Use local -r for constants.
guardrail.good: process_file() { local file="$1" local -r max_lines=1000 local line_count line_count="$(wc -l < "$file")" if (( line_count > max_lines )); then echo "Warning: $file exceeds $max_lines lines" >&2 fi }

guardrail.rule: Errors must go to stderr. Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = general error, 2 = usage error. Never use set +e — restructure logic instead.
Never use for file in $(find ...) — breaks on spaces. Use null-delimited read with find -print0 instead.
guardrail.bad: for file in $(find "$dir" -name "*.log"); do process "$file"; done
guardrail.good: while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do process "$file" done < <(find "$dir" -type f -name "*.log" -print0)

guardrail.rule: Use command -v instead of which for executable checks. Use $(command) instead of backticks. Use printf over echo for portable output.
POSIX scripts must not use bash-specific features ([[ ]], arrays, local). Use #!/bin/sh shebang for POSIX-only scripts.

script-structure.description: Standard structure for production shell scripts.

pattern.name: Parameter Expansion
pattern.example:
db_host="${DB_HOST:-localhost}" # Default value api_key="${API_KEY:?Error: API_KEY required}" # Required (fail if unset)
filename="archive.tar.gz" name="${filename%%.*}" # "archive" (longest suffix removal) ext="${filename#*.}" # "tar.gz" (shortest prefix removal) path="/usr/local/bin/tool" dir="${path%/*}" # "/usr/local/bin" base="${path##*/}" # "tool" upper="${var^^}" # UPPERCASE (Bash 4+) lower="${var,,}" # lowercase (Bash 4+)

pattern.name: Trap for Cleanup
pattern.example: cleanup() { local exit_code=$? rm -f "$tmpfile" exit "$exit_code" # Preserve original exit code } trap cleanup EXIT trap 'echo "Interrupted" >&2; exit 130' INT TERM

pattern.name: Arrays (Avoid eval)
pattern.example:
declare -a files=() files+=("first.txt" "second.txt") for file in "${files[@]}"; do echo "$file"; done
# Build commands safely with arrays cmd=(curl --silent --fail) [[ -n "${TOKEN:-}" ]] && cmd+=(--header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN") "${cmd[@]}" "$url"

pattern.name: Here Documents
pattern.example:
cat <<EOF # Interpolated Hello, $USER at $(hostname) EOF
cat <<'EOF' # Literal (no expansion) This $variable stays literal. EOF

pattern.name: Safe Temp Files
pattern.example: tmpfile="$(mktemp)" || exit 1 trap 'rm -f "$tmpfile"' EXIT umask 077 # Before creating sensitive files

pattern.name: Safe File Iteration (handles spaces and special characters)
pattern.example:
while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do process "$file" done < <(find "$dir" -type f -name "*.log" -print0)
# Simple globs (Bash 4+) shopt -s nullglob globstar for file in "$dir"/**/*.sh; do process "$file"; done

rules.rule: Test files in test/ or spec/ directory
Test names describe behavior: "deploy requires environment argument"
Use setup/teardown for temp dirs and fixtures

tooling.commands: shellcheck script.sh # Single file lint find . -name "*.sh" -exec shellcheck {} + # Lint all scripts shfmt -w -i 4 -bn script.sh # Format in place (4-space indent) shfmt -d -i 4 script.sh # Check only (diff output) bats test/ # Run tests bash -n script.sh # Syntax check (no execution)

quick-reference.item: NEVER — use arrays for dynamic command building
Never in script files; read from environment or secret managers
mktemp + trap EXIT; never hardcode /tmp paths
Always local; use local -r for constants
find -print0 + while IFS= read -r -d ''; never for in $(find)
command -v not which; $() not backticks; printf not echo
Zero warnings before commit; suppress with SC code comment
bats-core; setup/teardown per test; test/ or spec/ directory
